Article Title: Can reputation of a celebrity be inherited, asks HC
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court , which has recently become the preferred place to secure "personality rights", has raised concerns over the expanding nature of such rights.While hearing a suit filed in 2023 over "misleading" YouTube content about the health and private life of Aradhya Bachchan, the minor daughter of actors Abhishek Bachchan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, the HC questioned whether a family's reputation flows down generations, how far personality rights extend and whether even "egregiously despicable" fake news can violate intellectual property rights."A certain last name has a reputation because of its eminence in a certain field of work. So, does that reputation, that you are couching as virtually as a trademark, flow down generationally? If so, up to what point?" Justice Anup J Bhambhani asked, flagging points that need to be examined in such cases.In 2023, a single-judge bench had restrained several YouTube channels from publishing misleading content on Aaradhya's health, calling such misinformation about a child "morbid perversity" and "completely intolerable in law", and saying every child is entitled to respect.- Abhinav Garg
Article Summary: The Delhi high court has raised concerns over the expanding nature of "personality rights" The court questioned whether a family's reputation flows down generations. The court also questioned whether even "egregiously despicable" fake news can violate intellectual property rights.

Article Title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
Article Text:
SC gave the government two weeks to take a final call on introducing warning labels for packaged foods.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI ) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention."This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings."Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.The court, however, was unconvinced.The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions. The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness."In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings."We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI."The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.The issue has also been discussed by Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation, headed by Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora, who has advocated studying Singapore's Nutri-Grade model as a possible template for India.Separately, the Union health ministry has proposed displaying "sugar and oil boards" in schools, offices and other public institutions as part of a broader effort to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce excessive consumption of sugar and oil.
Article Summary: Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record. The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children. The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed “strong disapproval” of the Bar Council of India’s (BCI) now-revoked order barring the enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad’s NALSAR University of Law as advocates after a section of students objected to the university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.Kant, heading a bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said students have a right to protest peacefully and described the episode as a “dialogue” between him and the students."If students are protesting peacefully, who is BCI to take action? It is the right of the students to protest peacefully. It is a dialogue between students and me. No one else has to step in," the CJI said.Expressing its strong disapproval, the Supreme Court also stayed any coercive action against students or faculty by BCI or state Councils."It (the letter) was absolutely uncalled for," the bench added.The bench posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.On Thursday, the BCI had directed all state bar councils not to enrol any 2026 graduate of NALSAR University of Law as an advocate until further orders. It withdrew the directive within hours following an uproar on social media.In its initial statement, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council was examining allegations regarding a campaign against CJI Kant’s participation in the university’s convocation and had sought a report identifying those responsible.The BCI later modified its decision and allowed state bar councils to enrol the university’s 2026 graduates as advocates before withdrawing the notification altogether.The revised notification stated that the “vast majority” of students were innocent and should not be made to suffer for the alleged “misconduct” of a few.Around 450 graduating students of NALSAR had urged the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his alleged refusal to hear pleas concerning “police brutality” against students who had marched to Parliament on July 20 seeking the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG question paper leak in May. Pradhan’s resignation on July 25 brought the protests to an end.
Article Summary: Supreme Court expresses "strong disapproval" of Bar Council of India's now- revoked order. BCI had barred enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law as advocates. Students objected to university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.

Article Title: Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
Article Text:
Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment

NEW DELHI: “The elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.” Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.“Based on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),” Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems — pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says “at (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfaces” due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. “Since load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,” the communication says.“...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,” it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and France’s accident investigator under the ambit of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.
Article Summary: Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities. Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.

Article Title: Park outside your Bengaluru home? It may soon cost up to Rs 25,000 a year
Article Text:
Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking (File photo enhanced with AI)

Rules propose

Private operators to enforce rules

Common parking portal planned

Penalties prescribed

Illegal parking on roads

Rs 500 for cars

Rs 300 for two-wheelers

Parking on footpaths

Rs 1,000 for cars

Rs 600 for two-wheelers

Key conditions

Residential street parking allowed only through permit

Permit valid for one year

Parking outside the permitted area will be treated as a violation





BENGALURU: The city is all set to put a price on one of its most contested public resources, road space.Under the proposed Greater Bengaluru Authority Parking Rules, 2026, residents who want to park their cars on the road outside their homes will have to obtain annual permits, with fees varying by vehicle type.The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and Metro stations.There are proposals for a complete ban on parking on arterial roads identified as high-density corridors by Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).It also seeks parking restrictions during peak hours on select arterial roads notified by traffic police.In addition, vehicles would not be allowed to park near junctions, bus stops, transit hubs, pedestrian crossings and footpaths, with detailed setback requirements prescribed under the rules.The proposed rules seek to significantly reduce on-street parking near public transport hubs.Initially, on-street parking would be prohibited within 150 metres of Metro and suburban railway station boundaries. The draft allows city corporations to gradually increase the no-parking zone up to 500 metres.The proposal is expected to impact several high-footfall Metro station areas across the city where commuters currently rely on adjoining roads for parking.In a shift from the current system, the draft proposes to authorise private operators managing public parking facilities to issue violation notices, collect parking-related charges, tow vehicles and clamp vehicles after being formally authorised by city corporations.The operators would be required to record video evidence of violations before towing vehicles, and all towing activities would be overseen by traffic police.To increase organised parking supply, the draft allows city corporations to lease vacant private plots and develop them into public parking facilities.Private landowners who voluntarily convert vacant plots into parking facilities would be eligible for incentives, including property tax exemptions.Owners providing mechanised or multi-level parking facilities could receive 100% exemption from property tax and service charges, while owners offering surface-level parking could receive a 50% exemption.The draft directs Metro, BMTC and suburban rail agencies to create off-street parking facilities on land available with them, particularly at interchange stations and peripheral locations, to encourage park-and-ride travel.Transit agencies may also offer discounted parking rates for commuters using public transport.All parking operators, city corporations and transit agencies would be required to share real-time information on parking availability, occupancy and pricing with GBA.The data would eventually be integrated into a common citywide parking portal and mobile application to help motorists locate available parking spaces and enable authorities to plan future parking infrastructure.Traffic police will continue to have powers to enforce no-parking regulations, tow vehicles and take action against repeat offenders.The draft also allows city corporations to increase parking rates based on demand and location and proposes higher charges for longer parking durations to discourage all-day occupation of valuable road space.
Article Summary: Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking. Residents will have to obtain annual permits, with fees varying by vehicle type. The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and Metro stations.

Article Title: At BCI helm for 14 years, Manan Kumar Mishra faces heat over professional conduct
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BCI's controversial decision to bar 2026 law graduates from Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law from being registered as advocate, which it withdrew within hours, brought into focus the regulator's working which has been headed by senior advocate and BJP MP Manan Kumar Mishra for 14 years.A statutory body established under Advocates Act, 1961, BCI is mandated to regulate legal profession and legal education. It lays down standards of professional conduct for advocates, exercises disciplinary jurisdiction, and recognises universities whose law degrees qualify a person for enrolment. Section 7(1)(g) of the Act also gives it general supervision and control over state bar councils.But no provision of the Act gives it the power to enrol a person as an advocate which is to be done by a state bar council to admit persons as advocates on its roll. Clearly, the regulator ventured into the area beyond its domain by taking punitive measures against students, and upset SC which observed that BCI had no business to intervene in the matter.The controversy has put the spotlight on BCI's functioning on whether it has over the years been able to discharge its statutory duty to maintain the standard of legal profession and legal education. Going by a statement of Mishra himself, BCI has failed in its duty by a massive margin.An outspoken man who contested polls as nominees of BSP and Congress before drifting into BJP , has said on more than one occasion that 35-40% of advocates have fake degrees, and are practicing in the courts on the basis of fabricated degree certificates. The statement, while believed to be true by many, is an indictment of regulator and clear evidence that guard rails against serious malpractice have not been working.Another failure of BCI is in the field of legal education as it failed to maintain standard in view of proliferation of law colleges; some of them are virtually selling law degrees with students exempted from attending classes. It has regularly faced SC's ire for not infusing professionalism into the profession and not taking action against erring lawyers who keep resorting to strikes.
Article Summary: BCI's decision to bar 2026 law graduates from Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law from being registered as advocate has brought into focus the regulator's working. BCI has been headed by senior advocate and BJP MP Manan Kumar Mishra for 14 years.

NEW DELHI: A parliamentary panel has taken note of a curious case involving emergency alert buttons in buses. While the switches cost just Rs 15-20 each, they have largely remained unused because there are no dedicated centres to respond to alerts. Bus operators told the panel they are still required to pay Rs 2,500 to Rs 25,000 per vehicle to have the switches tested during mandatory fitness tests.The latest report of the parliamentary standing committee on transport, tourism and culture, headed by JDU's Sanjay Jha, noted that the buttons were made mandatory after the 2012 Nirbhaya case as a safety measure for women passengers.The report said the road transport ministry informed the panel that in several states, the system had been connected to emergency response number 112. It also said there were many instances of false alarms, prompting some states to "disengage" them."The ministry wishes the system restored, while am-ong operators there is a feeling that it should be dispensed with," the report said. A committee member observed if the system was not effective, it was not fair to charge so much for it. One member asked why CCTV could not be installed. The ministry said cameras were being made mandatory in new buses.The committee recommended that the programme to install emergency buttons, call facilities and vehicle location tracking devices in public transport vehicles be pursued with states beyond the 16 that have made progress in implementing it.
Article Summary: A parliamentary panel has taken note of a curious case involving emergency alert buttons in buses. While the switches cost just Rs 15-20 each, they have largely remained unused. Article Title: Armed Naxals gone, now identify & isolate 'dimagi Naxals': PM Modi on Independence Day
Article Text:
Govt to offer youth free online coaching for exams

New Delhi: The youth took centre stage in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day address on Saturday as he unveiled a host of initiatives, including free online coaching and AI skilling, but also warned against "dimagi Naxals. ..looking for ways of violence and anarchy", who, he said, must be "identified" and "isolated".The PM's 13th consecutive speech from the ramparts of Red Fort, over 75 minutes long, was marked by repeated invocations of the youth, who were the face of the most consequential protest his govt has faced since 2014, leading to education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation and a slew of legislative and executive measures to reform the examination system.The PM emphasised the threat "dimagi Naxals" pose even as his govt has largely eliminated "hathiyari Naxals" (armed Naxals). Modi has often used the term "urban Naxals" to describe sympathisers of the Maoist movement. His coinage of "dimagi Naxals" appears to be a nod to the belief in BJP circles that hardcore Left groups, especially AISA, the student wing of CPI(ML), played a key role in mobilising and sustaining support for the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest."These dimagi Naxals are looking for ways of violence and anarchy. They are resorting to various tactics to drag society to the wrong path. We must identify these dimagi Naxals, isolate them, and steer the nation's youth toward the mainstream effort of transforming India into a developed nation," he said.The challenge of 'dimagi Naxals should not be underestimated' as they used to have presence in "corridors of power", even as advisers in govt committees, he emphasised. BJP has accused Congress of keeping people with professed Naxal sympathies in committees that shaped policies during UPA's tenure in 2004-2014.PM Narendra Modi has himself revved up engagement with Gen Z of late, and used the showpiece annual event, in which he often lays out his governance agenda and sums up the country’s development arc since he took office in 2014, to unpack several programmes for them. This comes amid the assessment in political circles that there is a growing clamour for more and better job opportunities.Self-reliance was another key theme, with Modi announcing “sapta-dhara”, which will focus on seven different aspects of the country’s economy to ramp up growth.Fresh off a Parliament session, which was a virtual washout owing to the opposition’s protest against his govt on a variety of issues, Modi denounced his rivals as a bunch of doomsayers who draw perverse pleasure in keeping the country scared and worried, noting that they predicted the worst of fuel crises after the West Asia conflict broke out but his govt handled it ably. “Rumours were spread that petrol would not be available at petrol pumps, that there would be no gas, no diesel and no fertiliser,” he said.Acknowledging the financial burden of coaching classes on the poor and middle-class families, he announced, “We have decided to provide free online coaching for various examinations for the youth. We have digital public infrastructure; we have excellent talent and teachers.By bringing these resources together, we are going to build a complete network to provide free coaching to the youth of the country.”It will save these families thousands of crores of rupees and allow them to keep their children with them, he added.The PM had something for Gen Alpha as well: a nationwide talent hunt among children in 5-15 age bracket to give the selected players specialised training to prepare them as India looks to boost its standing in global sporting events. Govt will also develop a comprehensive civil defence programme, capable of addressing modern challenges and protecting citizens from contemporary crises, he said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi's Independence Day address was his 13th consecutive speech from the ramparts of Red Fort. He unveiled a host of initiatives, including free online coaching and AI skilling. But he also warned against "dimagi Naxals" who, he said, must be "identified" and "isolated"

Article Title: India and Bangladesh in talks for visit by PM Tarique Rahman next week
Article Text:

NEW DELHI/DHAKA: India and Bangladesh are discussing a possible bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman late next week, official sources said. Though the visit has yet to be officially confirmed, Rahman is likely to travel to India between Aug 21 and 25, in what would be his first trip to the country after taking office.PM Narendra Modi had invited Rahman for a bilateral visit and followed it up with another invitation to the Bangladesh PM in the latter’s capacity as the BIMSTEC chair for the BRICS summit that India will host in Sept.The two sides seem to agree that the bilateral visit could be more significant in advancing efforts to reset ties, which remain strained over several issues, including extradition of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina.According to diplomatic sources, other than Hasina, some of the issues that will likely weigh on Rahman’s mind while finalising his India trip include border management, domestic political optics, trade and visa normalisation, and water-sharing.For India, security concerns, including insurgent groups’ activities, protection of minorities and Dhaka’s potential tilt towards China and Pak, especially in defence and security, remain key issues.Ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, when asked about the proposed visit, said “We have extended an invitation to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh for a bilateral visit. We’ve also extended an invitation to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh for a visit to India for the outreach session of the BRICS Summit.So, these invitations have been extended, and I shall keep you updated if there is any progress in this regard,” Diplomatic sources in Dhaka said that despite opposition from domestic hardliners.Tarique Rahman is likely to visit India for the first time later this month, possibly on Aug 22-23. The dates are expected to be discussed further over the next two days.Sources also said that senior officials from both countries have been discussing a possible window between Aug 20 and 25. An engagement before Aug 28 is also being explored.
Article Summary: India and Bangladesh are discussing a possible bilateral visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman late next week. PM Narendra Modi had invited Rahman for a bilateral visit and followed it up with another invitation to the Bangladesh PM in the latter’s capacity as the BIMSTEC chair for the BRICS summit that India will host in Sept.

NEW DELHI: The food regulator failed to impose Rs 5.60 crore in penalties on 2,430 food businesses that either did not file or delayed filing mandatory annual returns, a CAG audit has found, raising questions over enforcement of basic food safety rules.An audit of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) Eastern Region office in Kolkata found that 1,018 food businesses did not submit their annual returns, while 1,412 filed them late during 2017-18 to 2022-23.These returns provide FSSAI with information on the quantities of food products manufactured, handled, imported or exported by licensed food businesses during the year. They have to be submitted by May 31. Businesses that miss the deadline are liable to pay a penalty of Rs 100 for each day of delay, subject to the prescribed limit.CAG estimated that Rs 5.60 crore in penalties should have been imposed on the 2,430 businesses. However, the audit found that FSSAI had not imposed the penalties. It also noted that none of the defaulters had their licence suspended or cancelled as of August 2023.Following the audit, FSSAI said improvement notices had been issued to some defaulting food businesses and that notices would be issued again to all defaulters.Of the Rs 5.60 crore penalty identified by CAG, Rs 2.27 crore had been recovered, according to the report.The finding is significant because filing an annual return is a basic requirement for licensed food businesses. The audit has highlighted gaps in FSSAI's monitoring and enforcement of this requirement.
Article Summary: 1,018 food businesses did not submit their annual returns, while 1,412 filed them late during 2017-18 to 2022-23. NEW DELHI: In an attempt to bridge gaps in access to specialist healthcare, 27 doctors from across Delhi have pledged two hours of free consultation every week for poor and underprivileged patients under a new volunteer initiative, '2 Ghante Desh Ke Naam'.The campaign brings together specialists from ophthalmology, oncology, orthopaedics, psychiatry, paediatrics, cardiology, gynaecology and general medicine, who will provide consultations free of cost through two hospitals and two clinics, as well as via telemedicine for patients in remote and underserved areas. Organisers said the initiative aims to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent patients from seeking timely medical advice.Unlike a centrally funded programme, the initiative is being run collectively by participating hospitals and clinics, each contributing voluntarily by dedicating doctors' time and infrastructure. Organisers said there is no single funding agency or institution leading the campaign.The programme seeks to reach patients from low-income families, rural areas and urban slums who often delay treatment because of cost or the lack of access to specialists.Besides consultations, doctors will also provide treatment guidance and follow-up advice where required. Patients will be able to register directly with participating specialists through dedicated contact numbers issued by each speciality, following which they will be screened and scheduled for consultations.Organisers said the digital component of the initiative would allow patients from smaller towns and villages to consult specialists without travelling long distances. They are also reaching out to medical associations and healthcare institutions across the country to encourage more doctors to volunteer and expand the initiative beyond Delhi."Many patients lose vision because they cannot access timely eye care. If doctors volunteer even a few hours each week, we can help prevent avoidable blindness among the poor," said Dr Ikeda Lal, senior ophthalmologist and medical director, Delhi Eye Centre.Dr L Tomar, senior orthopaedic surgeon and founder of Tomar Foundation, said, "Access to quality orthopaedic care should not depend on a person's ability to pay. Two hours of voluntary service every week can help reduce avoidable disability and improve quality of life."Highlighting the need for accessible mental healthcare, Dr Deepak Raheja, senior psychiatrist and director, Hope Care India, said, "Mental healthcare remains out of reach for many because of financial and social barriers. We want to ensure that those in need can access professional guidance without worrying about cost."Dr Ashish Gupta, chief of medical oncology at Amerix Multispecialty Hospital, said, "Cancer patients often delay treatment because of fear and financial constraints. Making specialist consultations free can encourage earlier diagnosis and timely treatment."
Article Summary: 27 doctors from across Delhi have pledged two hours of free consultation every week for poor and underprivileged patients. '2 Ghante Desh Ke Naam' campaign brings together specialists from ophthalmology, oncology, orthopaedics, psychiatry, paediatrics, cardiology, gynaecology and general medicine.

Article Title: CJI Surya Kant urges young lawyers to shoulder responsibility of future, says ‘much remains to be done’

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday said India had overcome several formidable challenges in the eight decades since Independence, but much remained to be done, urging young law graduates and lawyers to prepare themselves to shoulder the responsibilities of the future.Speaking at the national flag-hoisting ceremony organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association at the apex court premises on the occasion of India’s 80th Independence Day, Kant said the country’s achievements also brought with them a renewed sense of responsibility.“The journey of a nation does not end with what it has accomplished. Every achievement also brings with it a renewed sense of responsibility and duty. There is much that remains to be done, and many more miles to travel in our journey ahead,” he said.Several senior judges, lawyers and court staff attended the ceremony.Addressing young lawyers, Kant said the responsibility carried by the legal profession since the freedom struggle would soon pass to the next generation.“The responsibility that this Bar has carried since the days of the freedom struggle will, before long, rest on your shoulders.The institutions of justice that generations before you have built and strengthened are now yours to protect and to carry forward,” he said.He assured young lawyers that the Bar and Bench remained committed to supporting their professional growth through mentorship and opportunities.“The miles that remain are yours to walk, and we walk with you,” he added.Kant said the freedom struggle had a deep and enduring connection with law and that some of the finest legal minds of the period helped establish the idea that law should serve justice, protect liberty and uphold human dignity.He noted that Mahatma Gandhi and BR Ambedkar, whom he described as two of the greatest architects of modern India, along with Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Motilal Nehru, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Lala Lajpat Rai, were lawyers.This, he said, demonstrated that the legal profession was not a bystander to India's freedom struggle but an integral part of it.Kant said India's legal and judicial institutions had grown and matured alongside the Republic and played an important role in shaping the country's conscience.Turning to young lawyers, he acknowledged the difficulties of starting a legal career, saying the profession had become more competitive, the learning curve steeper and the pressure of building a practice heavier.“I personally remember the anxieties of those early years at the Bar, and I say this not to discourage our young colleagues, but because I want them to know that we see them, and we understand their challenges,” he said.At the same time, he expressed confidence in the younger generation, citing their resilience, intellect and commitment to justice.Kant said young lawyers had also grown up with technology transforming communication and access to knowledge, bringing greater adaptability to courtrooms. He also highlighted their sensitivity towards equality, inclusion and access to justice.Reflecting on India's freedom movement, the CJI said it differed from many earlier struggles against colonial rule because it was not primarily an armed insurrection.“Ours was not primarily an armed insurrection; it was instead a sustained challenge to the legitimacy of colonial rule through political movements, petitions, public debates, and, most importantly, through the language of law,” he said.He said the freedom movement repeatedly challenged the contradiction between colonial claims of governance through law and the denial of liberty, equality and dignity to Indians.According to Kant, that principle remains relevant today as courts provide a forum for people from different backgrounds to assert their constitutional rights, challenge arbitrary action and seek equal treatment under the law.“Courts have continued to serve as a unifying space for the litigants and members of the Bar alike,” he said.Supreme Court Bar Association president Vikas Singh and other members of the bar body also addressed the gathering.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said India had overcome several formidable challenges in the eight decades since Independence. He urged young law graduates and lawyers to prepare themselves to shoulder the responsibilities of the future. He spoke at the national flag-hoisting ceremony organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association at the apex court premises.

Article Title: 100GW of nuclear power by 2047, 5 reactors this decade: Inside PM Modi's energy self-reliance plan
Article Text:
Target of 100 GW of nuclear energy by 2047, 5 new nuclear reactors to be operational within 6-7 years: PM Modi

India enters second stage of three-stage nuclear programme

Why PFBR matters for India's nuclear expansion

Nuclear power seen as key to meeting rising electricity demand

India targets 500 GW renewable energy by 2030

SHANTI Act seeks to reshape India's nuclear power framework

India’s nuclear capacity to expand from 8.78 GW

Five reactors to be operationalised this decade

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nuclear power and India's 2070 net-zero target

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced an expansion of India's ambitious nuclear power programme, setting a target of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047.PM Modi said five new nuclear reactors would be operationalised during this decade as the country seeks greater energy security and self-reliance.Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India had taken an important step towards self-reliance in nuclear energy with the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu attaining first criticality in April this year.PM Modi said nuclear power would be an important component of India's energy security as demand for electricity rises with the expansion of technologies such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence and data centres. He also referred to the government's nuclear policy reforms and the SHANTI Act, enacted in December 2025, as part of efforts to expand the sector.“The new world cannot run without energy. Whether they are (semiconductor) chips, AI or data centres, the country needs lots of electricity … That’s why we have already taken strong steps to ensure energy security,” he added.PM Modi said India had set the goal of reaching 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, with five new reactors expected to become operational in the current decade.The PFBR at Kalpakkam marks India's entry into the second stage of its three-stage nuclear power programme, originally conceived by Homi J Bhabha.The 500 MWe reactor, developed and built indigenously at the Kalpakkam Nuclear Complex, attained first criticality on April 6, 2026. It is being built by Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited, or BHAVINI, under the Department of Atomic Energy, with technology developed by the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research.The first stage of India's nuclear programme relies on Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors, or PHWRs, which use natural uranium as fuel and produce plutonium as a byproduct.The second stage uses this plutonium in fast breeder reactors. The PFBR uses uranium-plutonium mixed oxide, or MOX, fuel and is designed to produce more fissile material than it consumes.The third stage of the programme is aimed at using India's large thorium reserves to produce uranium-233 for nuclear power generation.The PFBR is therefore intended to serve as a bridge between India's existing uranium-based nuclear programme and its longer-term thorium-based energy strategy.The PFBR is a 500 MWe sodium-cooled fast breeder reactor designed to use plutonium-based fuel while breeding additional fissile material.A blanket of uranium-238 around the reactor core can be converted into plutonium-239 through the action of fast neutrons. This allows the reactor to generate electricity while producing additional fuel.The reactor's technology is particularly relevant to India's nuclear strategy because the country has relatively limited uranium resources but substantial thorium reserves.The Department of Atomic Energy has said the PFBR will eventually help lay the foundation for the third stage of India's nuclear programme, in which thorium would be used to produce uranium-233.PM Modi had earlier described the PFBR milestone as a major development in India's civil nuclear programme.“Today, India takes a defining step in its civil nuclear journey, advancing the second stage of its nuclear programme.”PM Modi had also said, “This advanced reactor, capable of producing more fuel than it consumes, reflects the depth of our scientific capability and the strength of our engineering enterprise. It is a decisive step towards harnessing our vast thorium reserves in the third stage of the programme.”In his Independence Day address, PM Modi linked India's nuclear expansion with the country's rapidly increasing demand for electricity.He pointed to the growing power requirements of semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence and data centres, saying energy security would become increasingly important as India expands its technology and manufacturing sectors.“It is difficult to build a new world. That is why, whether it is a chip, AI, or data centre, we need electricity in large quantity. The new era demands energy.”PM Modi said India had taken steps to strengthen energy security by expanding both nuclear and renewable energy capacity.He said nuclear energy was vital for ensuring a stable supply of electricity while the country simultaneously expands solar, wind and other renewable sources.Alongside the nuclear expansion, PM Modi highlighted the growth of India's renewable energy capacity.He said India's solar energy capacity had risen from 2 GW in 2014 to 160 GW, while the country had set a target of 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.PM Modi also referred to the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, saying around 50 lakh households had been covered under the rooftop solar programme.Thousands of consumers, he said, were also earning through electricity generated from rooftop solar systems.Beneficiaries under the scheme can receive a subsidy of up to Rs 80,000 per household for installing rooftop solar systems.PM Modi also said India's railway electrification had expanded sharply, helping reduce diesel consumption and imports.He said India had also started work on a hydrogen train as part of its broader clean-energy transition.PM Modi also referred to the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India, or SHANTI Act, enacted in December 2025.The legislation is intended to modernise India's nuclear legal framework and facilitate greater participation in the nuclear sector under regulatory oversight.The law forms part of the government's broader effort to expand nuclear power capacity and bring new investment and technology into the sector.The Union Budget 2025-26 had also announced a Nuclear Energy Mission with an allocation of Rs 20,000 crore for the design, development and deployment of Small Modular Reactors.The government has set a target of having at least five indigenously designed small modular reactors operational by 2033.India's installed nuclear power capacity currently stands at around 8.78 GW, according to government data.Nuclear power accounted for about 3.1% of India's electricity generation in 2024-25, when nuclear plants generated 56,681 million units of electricity.The government has projected that India's nuclear capacity could reach around 22.38 GW by 2031-32 through the development of indigenous 700 MW reactors and larger reactors being developed through international cooperation.The 100 GW target by 2047 would therefore require a substantial expansion in both the number and scale of nuclear power projects over the next two decades.PM Modi said India would operationalise five nuclear reactors during the current decade as part of its push towards greater nuclear capacity.The expansion is expected to involve multiple reactor technologies, including India's indigenous PHWR designs and advanced reactor technologies.The government is also developing small modular reactor designs, including the 200 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor and the 55 MWe SMR-55, as well as other advanced reactor concepts.The expansion is aimed at increasing the contribution of nuclear energy to India's electricity mix while maintaining the country's broader clean-energy and net-zero commitments.The expansion of nuclear power is also linked to India's commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2070.Unlike solar and wind power, nuclear reactors can provide continuous electricity and are not dependent on weather conditions. This makes nuclear generation a potential source of firm, low-carbon electricity alongside renewable energy.The government has therefore positioned nuclear power as part of a wider energy mix that includes solar, wind, hydrogen and other clean-energy sources.PM Modi's announcement of the 100 GW target marks a substantial increase in India's long-term nuclear ambitions and places nuclear power at the centre of the country's energy security strategy as it works towards the Viksit Bharat 2047 goal.
Article Summary: PM Modi said five new nuclear reactors would be operationalised during this decade. The 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu attaining first criticality in April this year. PM Modi said nuclear power would be an important component of India's energy security.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said India had faced a series of crises over the past 10-12 years, including the COVID-19 pandemic and wars in Ukraine and West Asia, but maintained that a citizen-first approach helped the country navigate the challenges.Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on India’s 80th Independence Day, Modi said the country emerged from the pandemic only to confront a tense global environment.“In the last 10-12 years, we have faced many dangers. As soon as we emerged from Covid, there was news of wars that started to arise from Ukraine side and West Asia. An atmosphere of tension prevailed. God knows what all the predictions the predictors made!,” he said.PM Modi also accused some people of deliberately creating anxiety by spreading rumours about shortages of essential supplies during the pandemic.“Some people gain joy in keeping the nation terrified by spreading rumours that vaccines will not be available, petrol, diesel, and fertiliser will not be available in the country. Some people were gaining joy from creating an atmosphere of anxiousness in the country,” he said.He added, “Some people took delight in trying to terrify the people of India and plunge them into worry. Yet, the nation has witnessed how the well-conceived plans of the last 10-12 years are bearing fruit.”The Prime Minister said the government’s response to the pandemic was guided by the principle of “Nagrik Devo Bhava”, under which citizens remained the priority.Turning to development, Modi cited the expansion of piped gas infrastructure as an example of the changes achieved over the past 12 years.“12 years ago, piped gas lines were available in only 70 cities. In the last 12 years, this number has grown to 700 cities. Today, 1.75 crore households are connected to piped gas lines in the country,” he said.Modi also said India had made progress in eliminating Naxalism, while remembering security personnel killed in operations against the insurgency. He said more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed “in order to protect the people”.Further, in his 75-minutes speech from the Red Fort, the Prime Minister urged political parties to advance women’s representation in legislatures, calling for 33 per cent representation for women in state assemblies and the Lok Sabha.“Come forward and celebrate the strength and capability of our women,” Modi said, urging parties to “as swiftly as possible” ensure greater representation.He also expressed solidarity with families affected by recent floods and landslides, saying, “We, and the entire nation, stand with them.”
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi says India overcame crises through citizen-first governance and strategic planning. Modi also accused some people of deliberately creating anxiety by spreading rumours about shortages of essential supplies during the pandemic. He said more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed ‘in order to protect the people’

Article Title: AI, jobs, free coaching & sports: What PM Modi offered Gen Z on Independence Day

NEW DELHI: From artificial intelligence training for one crore young people to free online coaching for competitive examinations, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speech had several announcements aimed directly at India's youth, with technology, jobs, entrepreneurship and skills forming a key part of the message.Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India's youth would be the biggest beneficiary as well as the biggest enabler of the country's ambition to become a developed nation by 2047. He linked the Viksit Bharat goal to the country's young population and outlined initiatives spanning AI, education, sports, manufacturing and entrepreneurship.PM Modi announced that one crore youth would be trained in artificial intelligence-related skills. The announcement came as he described AI, quantum technology, robotics, space and data centres as defining technologies of the current era and called for India to become a global hub of innovation."When I speak of a developed India, when I speak of propelling the nation forward at a rapid pace, the greatest beneficiary and the greatest enabler of this vision is the youth of my country, the youthful energy of my nation.Not only that, but the greatest beneficiary of a developed India is also the youth of my country. Therefore, we must advance the goal of a developed India by linking it with our youth," PM Modi said.For students and young people preparing for government and other competitive examinations, PM Modi announced free online coaching. The initiative was among the youth-focused measures announced during the address.The prime minister also announced a nationwide sports talent hunt to identify and nurture children aged five to 15 years across villages and cities, expanding the focus on identifying sporting talent at an early age.AI was one of the biggest technology-related announcements in PM Modi's speech. He said one crore young people would receive training in AI skills as India seeks to build capabilities in emerging technologies.PM Modi placed the initiative within his broader 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara' framework, under which technology and innovation form the third stream of India's development strategy."The third strength of the Saptadhara is technology and innovation. This is the era of robotics, AI, quantum technology, space and data centres. Emerging technologies are presenting new challenges, and we must become a global hub of innovation," PM Modi said.He also pointed to India's existing digital infrastructure, including UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure, and said the country needed to take the next step in emerging technologies."We have already demonstrated our strength through UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure. Now, we must take the next leap in next-generation communication technology," he added.The AI training plan comes as PM Modi has repeatedly linked India's young workforce with the country's technology ambitions, with the latest announcement putting a specific focus on building AI-related skills at scale.For young people preparing for competitive examinations, PM Modi announced free online coaching.The initiative is aimed at making preparation resources available to youth without requiring them to rely exclusively on physical coaching centres.PM Modi said, "The race for coaching classes has become a massive burden for our middle-class families. Every parent feels that if they don't send their child to a coaching class, they aren't considered a 'prestigious' family. We are concerned about the thousands of crores of rupees these poor and middle-class families spend; we want to save them that expense. We have decided to provide free online coaching for various competitive exams for our youth. We have digital public infrastructure, as well as excellent talent and teachers. By leveraging these resources, we are establishing a comprehensive network to provide free coaching to the nation's youth."The announcement was made alongside the AI skilling plan as part of the government's broader focus on connecting India's youth with opportunities created by the country's development and technology push.PM Modi said the country's development target must be linked directly with young people, describing them as both the principal beneficiaries and enablers of Viksit Bharat.PM Modi also announced a nationwide sports talent hunt to identify and nurture children between five and 15 years of age.The programme will cover children in villages as well as cities, with the focus on identifying sporting talent at an early age and developing it further.The announcement adds sports to the list of areas through which the government plans to connect young Indians with the broader Viksit Bharat vision.PM Modi also referred to the growing role of women in sports, STEM education, aviation and the armed forces during his address.Beyond direct youth-focused announcements, PM Modi's seven-point roadmap placed manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power at the centre of India's growth strategy.For Gen Z entering the workforce, manufacturing and MSMEs were among the sectors PM Modi highlighted as areas with global opportunities.He urged Indian businesses, particularly MSMEs, to use free trade agreements to take Indian products to international markets."We have to reach the world. Everything that India produces should reach the world market," Modi said.PM Modi said Indian products in sectors such as textiles, machinery, pharmaceuticals, fisheries and seafood should expand their presence in global markets. He also stressed that companies would need to compete on international standards of cost, quality and scale.In manufacturing, PM Modi said India should become a reliable hub in global supply chains."From Design to Manufacturing, India must become a reliable hub in the global supply chain. For this, I want to place special emphasis on 3 things. My brothers and sisters in the field of Manufacturing, do not let this opportunity slip away. For this, we will have to meet global standards on cost, quality, and scale," PM Modi said.Technology and innovation were central to PM Modi's seven-point roadmap, with AI, quantum technology, robotics, space and data centres identified as areas where India should develop global capabilities."The third strength of the Saptadhara is technology and innovation. This is the era of robotics, AI, quantum technology, space and data centres. Emerging technologies are presenting new challenges, and we must become a global hub of innovation," PM Modi said.The prime minister also called for India to take the lead in next-generation communication technology, including 6G.For young entrepreneurs and technology professionals, PM Modi also spoke about the need for Indian technology companies to build globally recognised brands."India's technology companies should be a scoreboard in the world," he said.PM Modi's roadmap also identified defence production, the green economy and India's soft power as areas for future growth.In defence, he called for self-reliance and the development of next-generation defence technologies, with India aiming to become a global supplier."The importance of defence capability is paramount in every sense. My dear citizens, achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence is essential; India and the world have realised that there is no alternative. When the world looks out for itself, India cannot merely remain an arms market for other nations," he said.The sixth stream, the green and blue economy, covers renewable energy, energy storage, green manufacturing, fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology."The sixth strength of the Sapta Dhara is the Green economy. We must work in the areas of renewable energy, energy storage, green storage and manufacturing. India has an opportunity in the area of the Blue Economy. "The seventh stream is India's soft power, covering yoga, Ayurveda, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming and digital content."The seventh strength of the Sapta Dhara is India's soft power. Today, Yoga has connected the world to India. Our Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content. The world is recognizing and looking forward to India's WAVES summit. We have more than 100 national parks. We have an opportunity to attract foreign tourists through the power of soft power."PM Modi also used his Independence Day address to highlight India's economic transformation over the past 12 years, saying the country had moved from the 'Fragile Five' to becoming the world's fastest-growing major economy.He said India was now aiming for a larger role in global manufacturing, technology and trade and set out a goal of building Viksit Bharat by 2047.PM Modi cited growth in defence production, electronic manufacturing, railway coach production, internet use and digital transactions as indicators of the country's economic and technological expansion.He also announced that India had begun production at three semiconductor plants, with five to eight more plants expected to come up in the coming years.For Gen Z, the message running through PM Modi's youth-focused announcements was centred on acquiring skills in emerging technologies, accessing education and competitive-exam preparation, identifying sporting talent and participating in sectors that the government has identified as drivers of India's growth.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speech had several announcements aimed directly at India's youth. PM Modi announced that one crore youth would be trained in artificial intelligence-related skills. He also announced a nationwide sports talent hunt to identify and nurture children aged five to 15 years.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced “Sapta Dhara” - a seven-point reform framework that will accelerate India’s march towards its goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047.Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi recalled the era when India's might was known through the "Sapta Sindhu" and said the country now needs new streams of strength to build a developed India."Today, from the ramparts of the Red Fort, I invoke the seven streams of power before the nation," PM Modi said and identified seven areas of focus."In the coming 5-7 years, with the strength and power of these seven streams, we will give the country new heights, new momentum, and the capacity to achieve new goals," PM Modi said, adding that the full potential of the nation's youth power will be utilised in nation-building.The first strength of the 'Sapta Dhara' is manufacturing power, PM Modi said, stressing the need to take the manufacturing sector forward and produce both small components and large products. "We must build a complete value chain. From design to manufacturing, India must establish itself as a trusted global supply chain partner for the world," he said."We must rise to global standards of cost, quality and scale," the Prime Minister said.He said Indian manufacturers must meet global benchmarks on cost, quality and scale, while factories should be competitive, products user-friendly and packaging attractive."For every manufacturer, every entrepreneur, every MSME, I want to say that in the global market, our identity should be based on trust and quality," PM Modi said, stressing that there should be "no compromise" on quality.PM Modi defined the second stream as agriculture and food processing and called Indian farmers to access global markets."The world's markets are now open for our farmers. Due to FTAs, we are gaining access to a very large market. We must reach there," PM Modi said, stressing the need to go "from the farm to the export market".The Prime Minister said traditional cuisine, millets, spices, fruits and flowers and chemical-free agricultural produce could become global brands, provided they meet international parameters.Stating the third stream as technology and innovation, PM Modi said India must become an innovation hub as emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres create new opportunities."We have made our mark in UPI and digital public infrastructure," PM Modi said, calling for India's digital public technologies to be taken to every corner of the world."India must lead in next-generation communication technology. Made in India 6G should reach every corner; this should be our goal," PM Modi said.Defining the fourth strength of the 'Sapta Dhara' as Gati Shakti, PM Modi stressed the need for seamless and high-speed connectivity. "Our cities must be connected through high speed rail," he said.PM Modi also called for a focus on port-led development, saying ports should not remain merely places for loading and unloading goods but should become engines of growth.The PM highlighted defence power as the fifth strength, stressing the need for self-reliance in the defence sector and for India to emerge as a global supplier of next-generation defence technologies."When the world is thinking about itself, India cannot remain merely a market for the world," he said."We have to become global suppliers. We have to take leadership in hypersonic defence technologies," PM Modi said.He also called for developing drones, counter-drone systems and hypersonic defence technologies, while underlining the growing importance of cyber security. "India has to become self-reliant in the defence sector."PM Modi said the sixth stream is the green and blue economy, which will also create green jobs.He called for India to operate at a global scale in green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility and green manufacturing, while continuing to provide solutions to global challenges.The Prime Minister also highlighted opportunities in the blue economy, including fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology, given India's long coastline.The seventh stream is India's soft power, PM Modi said highlighting the global reach of yoga and India's strengths in faith and spiritual centres, Ayurveda and holistic healthcare."Yoga is becoming an energy for the world and a major source of confidence for India," the Prime Minister said.He said the 'Heal in India' movement, handicrafts, culture, films, VFX, animation, gaming and digital content are among the areas where India can build global strength.The Prime Minster also called for greater efforts to attract foreign tourists, noting that India has vast forest resources and more than 100 national parks but has not fully tapped its potential to attract international visitors.Prime Minister Modi stressed that the seven streams should not be viewed as separate sectoral initiatives."The seven powers of 'Sapta Dhara' are not meant to make progress in just one sector," he said, adding that India needs to adopt a "holistic approach" to achieve its development ambitions and cross the scale of the targets it has set for itself.The combined strength of the seven streams will help India achieve new heights and accelerate its progress towards the goal of becoming a developed nation, the Prime Minister asserted.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday announced “Sapta Dhara’ - a seven-point reform framework that will accelerate India’s march towards its goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047. The first strength of the 'SaptA Dhara' is manufacturing power, PM Modi said, stressing the need to take the manufacturing sector forward and produce both small components and large products.

Step forward in honour of our women, and as swiftly as possible, ensure our mothers and sisters receive 33% representation in the State Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha so that they can actively contribute to shaping India’s policies,” the prime minister said.PM Modi also highlighted the contribution of women representatives in various elected bodies and pointed to the passage of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in Parliament aimed at strengthening women’s representation in politics.“My dear fellow citizens, today in Panchayats, Municipalities, and Municipal Corporations, our women public representatives are guiding the nation in very large numbers, solving local challenges, and providing exceptionally capable and empowering leadership.Keeping this in mind, we passed the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in Parliament,” he added.However, he noted that “for one reason or another”, in the political arena over the last 40 years, the dream of greater representation for women had “persistently fallen victim to political games and political battlegrounds.”The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023, was passed by both Houses of Parliament but has not moved ahead with implementation after the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill fell in the Lok Sabha on April 17, failing to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting.The Bill proposed implementing 33% reservation for women in legislatures and delimiting Lok Sabha constituencies.

Article Title: SC concerned by continuance of derogatory witch-hunting practice
Article Text:
The Supreme Court of India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: More than 75 years of the Constitution coming into force, the derogatory practice of witch-hunting that targets defenceless women due to prejudice, suspicion, superstition and irrational fear, continues in the country, the Supreme Court lamented while upholding life term for two who murdered a woman in a tribal village of Odisha in Feb 1998.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria said the facets of the case had a disturbing impact on the court as a defenceless woman was branded a practitioner of witchcraft and was brutally assaulted in front of her daughter. “What effect it must have had on the daughter of the deceased who had to witness her mother being killed in the most brutal way,” the bench wondered.Writing the judgment, Justice Mishra said the malady of with-hunting continues to plague sections of our society, where prejudice, superstition, and irrational dear supersede the rule of law and constitutional morality.“The brutality associated with witch-hunting extends far beyond the act of killing; where victims mostly women are subjected to torture, beatings, sexual violence and social ostracization. In such a situation, superstitious beliefs or fears are given precedence leading to vulnerable women becoming victims of collective hostility,” he said.IN Feb 1998, in the remote village of tribal inhabited Sundergarh district, one Manobodha Naik’s daughter died, and family members claimed that she died because of witchcraft practice of one Puni Naik.Hearing this Udai Oram dragged Puni Naik to Naik’s house and with his associate, mercilessly assaulted her with sticks leading to her death. The trial court had convicted the duo in 2002, but the Orissa HC took two decades to uphold the conviction and life sentence.Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, “Sometimes in the most difficult situations, it often becomes an easy escape to blame a woman for the acts she did not commit, thus reflecting a deeply rooted social prejudice that often seeks scapegoats rather than solutions. In such situations, what can be given an ascendency is ‘reason’ for reason is the only virtue that stands as a bulwark against collective irrationality.”SC said the Constitution guarantees equality, promotes fraternity and envisages citizens to adopt scientific temperament to rid the society of derogatory practices against women. “Despite this, practices such as witch-hunting continue to persist within a few sections of our society. A Constitutional democracy such as ours cannot survive; wherein such derogatory practices continue to elude the principles of rule of law and Constitutional morality,” it said.
Article Summary: Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria said the facets of the case had a disturbing impact on the court as a defenceless woman was branded a practitioner of witchcraft. “What effect it must have had on the daughter of the deceased who had to witness her mother being killed in the most brutal way,” the bench wondered.

NEW DELHI: The Joint Action Forum on Minorities that had led a delegation of representatives of Churches to meet Home Minister Amit Shah last week described the decision of the govt to refer the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 to a Joint Parliamentary Committee as a “positive step” that presents an “important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications”.A host of Church bodies last week met and urged home minister Amit Shah to either withdraw the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill or send it to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.In their representation to HM, the delegation representing Catholic, Protestant and Orthodox Churches from across India organised under Joint Action Forum on Minorities with DMK MP P Wilson as its chairperson, had sought that the Bill is withdrawn in entirety or in alternate be referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee together with a review of the working of the Principal FCRA Act 2010 itself".On Wednesday, Wilson in a statement on X thanked DMK President MK Stalin and all opposition parties in the Lok Sabha for their unified demand to withdraw the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, even though it was decided by a majority voice vote to refer it to the Joint Parliamentary Committee.“Although the govt has not agreed to withdraw the FCRA Bill 2026 entirely, the Union Government's decision to refer the Bill to the Joint Parliamentary Committee is a positive step,” he added.“This is a sensitive issue where a balance must be struck between the govt’s authority over financial control and the rights of minority institutions to receive charitable contributions. This funding supports schools, colleges, hospitals, and other public service institutions. The government will be unable to fund these activities if contributions cease,” he added.Wilson said that the referral of the Bill to the JPC presents an important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications. “We hope and expect that the Committee will listen to all stakeholders and carefully consider the constitutional, legal, and practical concerns raised by religious, educational, healthcare, charitable, and civil society institutions,” he said.The National Council of Churches in India, General Secretary, Asir Ebenezer welcomed the Bill and said that they look forward to engaging with “the JPC as they prepare the report for the Winter session”. NCCI was part of the delegation that met the HM as part of the Joint Action Forum on Minorities.“On behalf of the historic and nationally networked Protestant and Orthodox Churches in India representing the religious and mission aspirations of 19 million Christians we thank the Home Minister and the govt for heeding to the request of the Christian community,” he added.
Article Summary: A host of Church bodies last week met and urged home minister Amit Shah to either withdraw the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill or send it to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny. The decision to refer the bill to JPC was made by a voice vote.

NEW DELHI: CPM MP John Brittas on Wednesday alleged that BJP MP Sushmita Dev used a “derogatory” remark against him, accusing the former TMC and Congress leader of calling him a “lungi wala.”The issue was raised in the Rajya Sabha, where both leaders are MPs, triggering an uproar and prompting the House to adjourn till 2pm.“The other day, while I was speaking in the House, she made a derogatory remark, ‘lungi wala’, against me. I was wearing a dhoti, and I am proud to be a Malayali, proud to be a South Indian,” Brittas told ANI.The Rajya Sabha member added that while he was proud of his culture, such remarks amounted to “stereotypes” and were made in a “derogatory” manner."This is not acceptable. We do not call it lungi; we call it dhoti.”Union minister Kiren Rijiju echoed the call for maintaining the dignity of the House.“Every member is equal in the House, and if there is anything unbecoming of the dignity of the House, the Chairman may call the members to his Chamber and hear them out,” Rijiju remarked, adding that since the allegations were directed at a specific member, Dev should also be heard.Taking note of the exchange, Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan urged members to maintain decorum and respect regional sensibilities.“Hon'ble Members, certain instances have come to my notice regarding discourteous and undignified comments being made by Members interrupting the speech of other Members in the House. I would advise that Hon'ble Members should be careful not to hurt the sentiments and feelings of fellow Members,” he observed.Emphasising the inclusive nature of Indian society, the Chairman added, “Our culture is unique and inclusive of diverse regional cultures. There should be no disrespect to the cultural traditions and regional identities of our colleagues.”Radhakrishnan subsequently called the concerned members to his chamber to resolve the matter and ensure the smooth functioning of the House.

NEW DELHI: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry, even as its total receipts between the date of announcement and completion of these polls stood at Rs 207.1 crore.According to Congress's election expenditure statement for the five state/UT polls, filed on July 31 with the Election Commission, the party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft between March 15, 2026, when the elections were announced, and May 6, 2026, when they had concluded.The Congress's full poll expense statement shows its total opening balance of cash in hand (including at the level of its central headquarters and the state/district/local level units of the 5 states/UTs) at Rs 22.9 crore and its cash in bank at Rs 146.1 crore. At the end of the polls, its cash in hand was marginally lower at Rs 22.6 crore while its bank balance had declined by 45% to Rs 80.6 crore.On the expenditure side, the party declared a total spend of Rs 143 crore on general party propaganda and Rs 105.6 crore on candidates. The latter includes Rs 95.5 crore given by the party as lump-sum payments to its candidates across the five poll-gone states/UT; while the central party headquarters bore Rs 95.3 crore of expenditure under this head, the state/district/local units disbursed only Rs 23 lakh among the candidates.Expenses on virtual campaigns through social media platforms and applications were declared at Rs 6.8 crore.Over Rs 3.2 crore was spent by the Congress on publicising the criminal antecedents of its candidates.As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements, covering print and electronic space, bulk SMS, cable TV, websites and TV channels. Another Rs 8 crore funded public meetings, processions and rallies, while Rs 11.5 crore was spent on badges, posters, cutouts, hoardings etc and nearly Rs 2 crore on miscellaneous propaganda items.Poll surveys and campaigns for the five assembly elections cost the Congress Rs 4.8 crore.A total Rs 23.5 crore was spent by the grand old party on the travel and lodging of its star campaigners (Rs 21.8 crore) and other leaders. The aircraft and helicopters were sourced from Air Charter Services Pvt Ltd, Aircab Aviation, A R Airways, GMP Air Charter, Lima Tang Aviation Service, Devigo Data Systems and Global Vectra.The Congress's central headquarters routed Rs 83.2 crore of its lump-sum payments to candidates through the state/UT units; with Kerala unit getting the largest share at Rs 55.1 crore, followed by Puducherry (Rs 10 crore), West Bengal (Rs 9 crore), Tamil Nadu (Rs 7.1 crore) and Assam (Rs 2 crore).The Congress-led UDF seized power in Kerala, but the party or its alliances performed poorly in other states, managing 21 seats in Assam, 6 in Puducherry and 2 in West Bengal, while drawing a blank in Tamil Nadu.
Article Summary: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections. The party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft. As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements.

Article Title: ‘MPs should not be reduced’: Udhayanidhi Stalin backs TVK's resolution against delimitation
Article Text:
DMK backs Tamil Nadu’s delimitation resolution
